title: Why we all need to practice emotional first aid
speaker: Guy Winch

sentences.en: I grew up with my identical twin, who was an incredibly loving brother.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同父异母的双胞胎一起长大 他是一个非常可爱的弟弟

sentences.en: Now, one thing about being a twin is, it makes you an expert at spotting favoritism.
sentences.zh: 现在,做双胞胎的一件事是, 它使你成为一个专家 发现偏袒。

sentences.en: If his cookie was even slightly bigger than my cookie, I had questions.
sentences.zh: 如果他的饼干比我的饼干大一点, 我有一些问题。

sentences.en: And clearly, I wasn't starving. (Laughter) When I became a psychologist, I began to notice favoritism of a different kind; and that is, how much more we value the body than we do the mind.
sentences.zh: 很明显,我没有饿。 当我成为一名心理学家时, 我开始注意到一种不同的偏爱, 也就是说,我们比我们更重视身体。

sentences.en: I spent nine years at university earning my doctorate in psychology, and I can't tell you how many people look at my business card and say, "Oh -- a psychologist. So, not a real doctor,"
sentences.zh: 我在大学学习了九年, 获得心理学博士学位, 我不能告诉你有多少人看我的名片, 说,“哦,心理学家。所以,不是一个真正的医生。”

sentences.en: as if it should say that on my card. [Dr. Guy Winch, Just a Psychologist (Not a Real Doctor)] (Laughter) This favoritism we show the body over the mind -- I see it everywhere.
sentences.zh: 仿佛这应该在我的名片上说。 [盖伊·温奇医生,只是一个心理学家(不是真正的医生)] (笑声)这种偏爱我们把身体展示在脑海——我到处都能看到。

sentences.en: I recently was at a friend's house, and their five-year-old was getting ready for bed.
sentences.zh: 我最近去了朋友家 他们的5岁小孩准备睡觉了

sentences.en: He was standing on a stool by the sink, brushing his teeth, when he slipped and scratched his leg on the stool when he fell.
sentences.zh: 他站在水槽旁的凳子上刷牙,他滑倒时在凳子上抓伤了腿。

sentences.en: He cried for a minute, but then he got back up, got back on the stool, and reached out for a box of Band-Aids to put one on his cut.
sentences.zh: 他哭了一分钟,但后来他又站起来, 回到凳子上, 并伸出手 拿出一盒创可贴在他的伤口上。

sentences.en: Now, this kid could barely tie his shoelaces, but he knew you have to cover a cut so it doesn't become infected, and you have to care for your teeth by brushing twice a day.
sentences.zh: 这孩子几乎连鞋带都绑不住 但他知道你得补上伤口 以免感染 你每天刷两次牙 才能照顾好你的牙齿

sentences.en: We all know how to maintain our physical health and how to practice dental hygiene, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都知道如何保持身体健康 以及如何练习牙科卫生,对不对?

sentences.en: We've known it since we were five years old.
sentences.zh: 我们五岁时就知道了

sentences.en: But what do we know about maintaining our psychological health?
sentences.zh: 但我们对维持我们的心理健康了解多少?

sentences.en: Well, nothing. What do we teach our children about emotional hygiene?
sentences.zh: 没什么,我们该怎么教孩子 情绪卫生?

sentences.en: Nothing. How is it that we spend more time taking care of our teeth than we do our minds?
sentences.zh: 没什么,我们怎么花更多的时间 来照顾我们的牙齿?

sentences.en: Why is it that our physical health is so much more important to us than our psychological health?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们的身体健康比我们的心理健康更重要?

sentences.en: We sustain psychological injuries even more often than we do physical ones, injuries like failure or rejection or loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我们遭受的心理伤害甚至比身体伤害、失败或排斥或孤独更频繁。

sentences.en: And they can also get worse if we ignore them, and they can impact our lives in dramatic ways.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不理会它们,它们也会变得更糟,而且它们会以戏剧性的方式影响我们的生活。

sentences.en: And yet, even though there are scientifically proven techniques we could use to treat these kinds of psychological injuries, we don't.
sentences.zh: 然而,尽管有科学证明的技术 我们可以用来治疗这些心理伤害,但我们没有。

sentences.en: It doesn't even occur to us that we should.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至没有想到我们应该这么做。

sentences.en: "Oh, you're feeling depressed? Just shake it off; it's all in your head."
sentences.zh: "哦,你感觉很沮丧吗?

sentences.en: Can you imagine saying that to somebody with a broken leg: "Oh, just walk it off; it's all in your leg."
sentences.zh: 你能想象对断腿的人说: "哦,只是走下来,这一切都在你的腿。"

sentences.en: (Laughter) It is time we closed the gap between our physical and our psychological health.
sentences.zh: 是时候弥补我们身体和心理健康之间的差距了

sentences.en: It's time we made them more equal, more like twins.
sentences.zh: 是时候让他们更平等了 更像是双胞胎

sentences.en: Speaking of which, my brother is also a psychologist.
sentences.zh: 说到这个 我哥哥也是心理学家

sentences.en: So he's not a real doctor, either. (Laughter) We didn't study together, though.
sentences.zh: 所以他也不是真正的医生。

sentences.en: In fact, the hardest thing I've ever done in my life is move across the Atlantic to New York City to get my doctorate in psychology.
sentences.zh: 事实上,我这辈子最难的事 就是穿越大西洋到纽约市 获得心理学博士学位

sentences.en: We were apart then for the first time in our lives, and the separation was brutal for both of us.
sentences.zh: 那时我们第一次分开 分开对我们两个都是残酷的

sentences.en: But while he remained among family and friends, I was alone in a new country.
sentences.zh: 但是当他和家人和朋友在一起时 我独自在一个新的国家里

sentences.en: We missed each other terribly, but international phone calls were really expensive then, and we could only afford to speak for five minutes a week.
sentences.zh: 我们非常想念对方,但国际电话费真的很高,我们只能每周讲5分钟。

sentences.en: When our birthday rolled around, it was the first we wouldn't be spending together.
sentences.zh: 当我们的生日滚动, 这是第一个 我们不会花在一起。

sentences.en: We decided to splurge, and that week, we would talk for 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们决定大摇大摆, 并且那个星期, 我们将谈10分钟。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I spent the morning pacing around my room, waiting for him to call -- and waiting ...
sentences.zh: (笑声) 我花了早上的步伐 在我的房间周围, 等待他打电话 - 和等待...

sentences.en: and waiting. But the phone didn't ring. Given the time difference, I assumed, "OK, he's out with friends, he'll call later."
sentences.zh: 但电话没响,因为时间差,我想,"好吧,他和朋友出去了,他晚点再打来"

sentences.en: There were no cell phones then. But he didn't.
sentences.zh: 那时没有手机 但他没有

sentences.en: And I began to realize that after being away for over 10 months, he no longer missed me the way I missed him.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到,在离开10个多月后, 他不再像我那样想念他。

sentences.en: I knew he would call in the morning, but that night was one of the saddest and longest nights of my life.
sentences.zh: 我知道他早上会打电话来 但那晚是我一生中最悲伤 最漫长的夜晚之一

sentences.en: I woke up the next morning. I glanced down at the phone, and I realized I had kicked it off the hook when pacing the day before.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上我醒来,我看着电话, 发现我前天的节奏时 把它踢掉了。

sentences.en: I stumbled out of bed, I put the phone back on the receiver, and it rang a second later.
sentences.zh: 我从床上摔下来, 我把电话放回了接收器, 它响了一秒钟。

sentences.en: And it was my brother, and boy, was he pissed.
sentences.zh: 和我的兄弟, 和男孩,他生气了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) It was the saddest and longest night of his life as well.
sentences.zh: 这是他一生中最悲伤和最长的夜晚

sentences.en: Now, I tried to explain what happened, but he said, "I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 现在,我想解释发生了什么, 但他说,“我不明白。

sentences.en: If you saw I wasn't calling you, why didn't you just pick up the phone and call me?"
sentences.zh: 如果你看到我没有给你打电话, 为什么你不直接拿起电话打电话给我?”

sentences.en: He was right. Why didn't I call him? I didn't have an answer then.
sentences.zh: 他说得对,我为什么不打电话给他?

sentences.en: But I do today, and it's a simple one: loneliness.
sentences.zh: 但我今天做了,这是一个简单的: 孤独。

sentences.en: Loneliness creates a deep psychological wound, one that distorts our perceptions and scrambles our thinking.
sentences.zh: 孤独造成了深刻的心理创伤 扭曲了我们的看法 扰乱了我们的思维

sentences.en: It makes us believe that those around us care much less than they actually do.
sentences.zh: 它让我们相信,我们周围的人 关心的比他们实际关心的要少得多。

sentences.en: It make us really afraid to reach out, because why set yourself up for rejection and heartache when your heart is already aching more than you can stand?
sentences.zh: 它让我们真的害怕伸出手来, 因为为什么让你自己 被排斥和心痛 当你的心已经痛得要死?

sentences.en: I was in the grips of real loneliness back then, but I was surrounded by people all day, so it never occurred to me.
sentences.zh: 当时我非常孤独 但我整天被人包围 所以从没有想过

sentences.en: But loneliness is defined purely subjectively.
sentences.zh: 但孤独是完全主观的

sentences.en: It depends solely on whether you feel emotionally or socially disconnected from those around you.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于你是否感到 情感或社会上与你周围的人脱节。

sentences.en: And I did. There is a lot of research on loneliness, and all of it is horrifying.
sentences.zh: 我做了。有很多关于孤独的研究, 所有的都是可怕的。

sentences.en: Loneliness won't just make you miserable; it will kill you.
sentences.zh: 寂寞不会让你痛苦的,会杀了你的

sentences.en: I'm not kidding. Chronic loneliness increases your likelihood of an early death by 14 percent.
sentences.zh: 我不是在开玩笑 慢性孤独会增加你早死的可能性14%

sentences.en: Fourteen percent! Loneliness causes high blood pressure, high cholesterol.
sentences.zh: 14% 孤独导致高血压 高胆固醇

sentences.en: It even suppress the functioning of your immune system, making you vulnerable to all kinds of illnesses and diseases.
sentences.zh: 它甚至抑制了你的免疫系统, 使你容易受到各种疾病的影响。

sentences.en: In fact, scientists have concluded that taken together, chronic loneliness poses as significant a risk for your long-term health and longevity as cigarette smoking.
sentences.zh: 事实上,科学家们得出的结论是,长期孤独与吸烟一样,对你的长期健康和寿命构成重大风险。

sentences.en: Now, cigarette packs come with warnings saying, "This could kill you."
sentences.zh: 现在,烟盒来 警告说,"这可能会杀了你。"

sentences.en: But loneliness doesn't. And that's why it's so important that we prioritize our psychological health, that we practice emotional hygiene.
sentences.zh: 但是孤独是没有的。这就是为什么我们把心理健康放在优先地位, 并且我们进行情感卫生。

sentences.en: Because you can't treat a psychological wound if you don't even know you're injured.
sentences.zh: 因为你连自己受伤都不知道 就没法治疗心理创伤

sentences.en: Loneliness isn't the only psychological wound that distorts our perceptions and misleads us.
sentences.zh: 孤独并不是扭曲我们观念和误导我们的唯一心理创伤。

sentences.en: Failure does that as well. I once visited a day care center, where I saw three toddlers play with identical plastic toys.
sentences.zh: 失败也是一样。我曾经参观过日托中心, 在那里我看到三个小孩玩同样的塑料玩具。

sentences.en: You had to slide the red button, and a cute doggie would pop out.
sentences.zh: 你不得不滑动红色按钮, 和可爱的狗弹出。

sentences.en: One little girl tried pulling the purple button, then pushing it, and then she just sat back and looked at the box with her lower lip trembling.
sentences.zh: 一个小女孩试着拉紫色的按钮, 然后推它, 然后她就坐在后面, 看着盒子 与她的下唇颤抖。

sentences.en: The little boy next to her watched this happen, then turned to his box and burst into tears without even touching it.
sentences.zh: 她旁边的小男孩看着这一切发生,然后转过身去,流着眼泪,连碰都没碰过。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, another little girl tried everything she could think of until she slid the red button, the cute doggie popped out, and she squealed with delight.
sentences.zh: 同时,另一个小女孩尝试了一切 她可以想到,直到她滑 红色按钮,可爱的狗跳出来, 她尖叫高兴。

sentences.en: So: three toddlers with identical plastic toys, but with very different reactions to failure.
sentences.zh: 所以:三个小孩 与相同的塑料玩具, 但与失败的反应非常不同。

sentences.en: The first two toddlers were perfectly capable of sliding a red button.
sentences.zh: 头两个小孩 完全可以滑动一个红色按钮

sentences.en: The only thing that prevented them from succeeding was that their mind tricked them into believing they could not.
sentences.zh: 阻止他们成功的唯一原因就是 他们的头脑欺骗了他们 让他们相信他们不能成功

sentences.en: Now, adults get tricked this way as well, all the time.
sentences.zh: 现在,成人也会被骗 这样的方式,所有的时间。

sentences.en: In fact, we all have a default set of feelings and beliefs that gets triggered whenever we encounter frustrations and setbacks.
sentences.zh: 事实上,我们都有一种预设的感觉和信念,每当我们遇到挫折和挫折时就会触发这种感觉和信念。

sentences.en: Are you aware of how your mind reacts to failure?
sentences.zh: 你知道自己对失败的反应吗?

sentences.en: You need to be. Because if your mind tries to convince you you're incapable of something, and you believe it, then like those two toddlers, you'll begin to feel helpless and you'll stop trying too soon, or you won't even try at all.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你的大脑想说服你 自己是无能的, 并且你相信它, 然后像那两个小孩一样, 你会开始感到无助, 你会很快停止尝试, 或者你甚至不会尝试。

sentences.en: And then you'll be even more convinced you can't succeed.
sentences.zh: 然后你会更确信自己不能成功

sentences.en: You see, that's why so many people function below their actual potential.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这么多人 运行低于他们的实际潜力。

sentences.en: Because somewhere along the way, sometimes a single failure convinced them that they couldn't succeed, and they believed it.
sentences.zh: 因为在路上的某个地方 有时一个失败 让他们相信他们不能成功 他们相信了

sentences.en: Once we become convinced of something, it's very difficult to change our mind.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们被说服了 改变主意就很难了

sentences.en: I learned that lesson the hard way when I was a teenager with my brother.
sentences.zh: 我和弟弟在十几岁的时候 学到了这个教训

sentences.en: We were driving with friends down a dark road at night, when a police car stopped us.
sentences.zh: 晚上我们和朋友在黑暗的路上开车 一辆警车拦住了我们

sentences.en: There had been a robbery in the area and they were looking for suspects.
sentences.zh: 该地区发生了一起抢劫,他们正在寻找嫌疑人。

sentences.en: The officer approached the car, and shined his flashlight on the driver, then on my brother in the front seat, and then on me.
sentences.zh: 警官走近车门,用手电筒照射司机,然后用前座上的我弟弟,然后用手电筒照射我。

sentences.en: And his eyes opened wide and he said, "Where have I seen your face before?"
sentences.zh: 他睁开眼睛说:以前我在哪里见过你?

sentences.en: (Laughter) And I said, "In the front seat."
sentences.zh: 我说,"在前座。"

sentences.en: (Laughter) But that made no sense to him whatsoever, so now he thought I was on drugs.
sentences.zh: 但它没有任何意义 他现在以为我嗑药了

sentences.en: (Laughter) So he drags me out of the car, he searches me, he marches me over to the police car, and only when he verified I didn't have a police record, could I show him I had a twin in the front seat.
sentences.zh: 所以他把我从车里拖出来 搜身 把我送去警车 只有当他证实我没有警察记录时 我才能证明我前座有一个双胞胎

sentences.en: But even as we were driving away, you could see by the look on his face he was convinced that I was getting away with something.
sentences.zh: 但是,即使我们开车离开, 你可以看到他脸上的表情 他相信,我得到了 一些东西。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Our mind is hard to change once we become convinced.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 我们的思想很难改变 一旦我们被说服。

sentences.en: So it might be very natural to feel demoralized and defeated after you fail.
sentences.zh: 所以在你失败后 感觉情绪低落和失败 是很自然的

sentences.en: But you cannot allow yourself to become convinced you can't succeed.
sentences.zh: 但你不能让自己相信自己不能成功

sentences.en: You have to fight feelings of helplessness.
sentences.zh: 你必须对抗无助的感觉。

sentences.en: You have to gain control over the situation.
sentences.zh: 你必须控制局面

sentences.en: And you have to break this kind of negative cycle before it begins.
sentences.zh: 在这种消极循环开始之前 你必须打破它

sentences.en: [Stop Emotional Bleeding] Our minds and our feelings -- they're not the trustworthy friends we thought they were.
sentences.zh: 我们的思想和感情... 他们不是我们以为的值得信赖的朋友

sentences.en: They're more like a really moody friend, who can be totally supportive one minute, and really unpleasant the next.
sentences.zh: 他们更像一个很情绪化的朋友, 谁可以完全支持一分钟, 和真正的不愉快的下一秒。

sentences.en: I once worked with this woman who, after 20 years marriage and an extremely ugly divorce, was finally ready for her first date.
sentences.zh: 我曾和这个女人共事过 她结婚20年 离婚后 终于准备好第一次约会了

sentences.en: She had met this guy online, and he seemed nice and he seemed successful, and most importantly, he seemed really into her.
sentences.zh: 她在网上见过这个家伙 他看起来不错 他看起来很成功 最重要的是 他看起来对她很感兴趣

sentences.en: So she was very excited, she bought a new dress, and they met at an upscale New York City bar for a drink.
sentences.zh: 所以她很兴奋,买了件新衣服, 他们在纽约的一家高级酒吧碰头喝一杯。

sentences.en: Ten minutes into the date, the man stands up and says, "I'm not interested," and walks out.
sentences.zh: 约会10分钟后 那个人站起来说 "我没兴趣" 然后走人

sentences.en: Rejection is extremely painful. The woman was so hurt she couldn't move.
sentences.zh: 拒绝是非常痛苦的 那个女人受了很大伤 无法移动

sentences.en: All she could do was call a friend. Here's what the friend said: "Well, what do you expect?
sentences.zh: 她只能打电话给朋友 朋友说:"你期望什么?

sentences.en: You have big hips, you have nothing interesting to say.
sentences.zh: 你有大屁股, 你没有什么有趣的话要说。

sentences.en: Why would a handsome, successful man like that ever go out with a loser like you?"
sentences.zh: 为什么一个英俊的,成功的男子 像你这样的失败者会出去?"

sentences.en: Shocking, right, that a friend could be so cruel?
sentences.zh: 令人吃惊,对吗,一个朋友会这么残忍?

sentences.en: But it would be much less shocking if I told you it wasn't the friend who said that.
sentences.zh: 但是如果我告诉你 不是那个朋友说的 那会更不令人震惊

sentences.en: It's what the woman said to herself. And that's something we all do, especially after a rejection.
sentences.zh: 那是那个女人对自己说的 特别是被拒后

sentences.en: We all start thinking of all our faults and all our shortcomings, what we wish we were, what we wish we weren't.
sentences.zh: 我们都开始思考 我们所有的缺点和缺点, 我们希望我们是什么, 我们希望我们不是。

sentences.en: We call ourselves names. Maybe not as harshly, but we all do it.
sentences.zh: 我们叫自己名字,也许不那么严厉,但我们都这样做。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that we do, because our self-esteem is already hurting.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是,我们这样做, 因为我们的自尊心已经受到伤害了。

sentences.en: Why would we want to go and damage it even further?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要进一步破坏它呢?

sentences.en: We wouldn't make a physical injury worse on purpose.
sentences.zh: 我们不会故意把身体伤害弄得更糟

sentences.en: You wouldn't get a cut on your arm and decide, "Oh! I know -- I'm going to take a knife and see how much deeper I can make it."
sentences.zh: 你不会得到一个切伤 你的手臂,然后决定,“哦,我知道—— 我要拿一把刀,看看我能做得多深。”

sentences.en: But we do that with psychological injuries all the time.
sentences.zh: 但是,我们这样做 心理伤害所有的时间。

sentences.en: Why? Because of poor emotional hygiene. Because we don't prioritize our psychological health.
sentences.zh: 为什么 因为情绪卫生差 因为我们没有优先考虑我们的心理健康

sentences.en: We know from dozens of studies that when your self-esteem is lower, you are more vulnerable to stress and to anxiety; that failures and rejections hurt more, and it takes longer to recover from them.
sentences.zh: 我们从几十项研究中知道,当你的自尊心降低时,你更容易受到压力和焦虑;失败和拒绝伤害更多,从中恢复需要更长的时间。

sentences.en: So when you get rejected, the first thing you should be doing is to revive your self-esteem, not join Fight Club and beat it into a pulp.
sentences.zh: 所以当你被拒绝的时候,你应该做的第一件事 就是恢复你的自尊, 而不是加入战斗俱乐部 把它打成纸浆。

sentences.en: When you're in emotional pain, treat yourself with the same compassion you would expect from a truly good friend.
sentences.zh: 当你在感情上痛苦的时候, 以同样的同情心对待自己 你期望从一个真正的好友。

sentences.en: [Protect Your Self-Esteem] We have to catch our unhealthy psychological habits and change them.
sentences.zh: 我们必须抓住我们不健康的心理习惯,改变这些习惯。

sentences.en: And one of unhealthiest and most common is called rumination.
sentences.zh: 最不健康最常见的就是光彩亮丽

sentences.en: To ruminate means to chew over. It's when your boss yells at you or your professor makes you feel stupid in class, or you have big fight with a friend and you just can't stop replaying the scene in your head for days,
sentences.zh: 当你的老板对你或者你的教授大喊大叫 让你在课堂上感到愚蠢, 或者你和一个朋友大吵大闹

sentences.en: sometimes for weeks on end. Now, ruminating about upsetting events in this way can easily become a habit, and it's a very costly one, because by spending so much time focused on upsetting and negative thoughts,
sentences.zh: 有时在最后几个星期内。现在,用这种方式来反省令人沮丧的事件很容易成为一种习惯, 这是一种非常昂贵的习惯, 因为花这么多的时间 来专注于烦恼和消极的想法,

sentences.en: you are actually putting yourself at significant risk for developing clinical depression, alcoholism, eating disorders, and even cardiovascular disease.
sentences.zh: 事实上,你将自己置于极大的风险 临床抑郁症,酗酒,饮食失调,甚至心血管疾病。

sentences.en: The problem is, the urge to ruminate can feel really strong and really important, so it's a difficult habit to stop.
sentences.zh: 问题在于 调情的冲动 感觉非常强烈 并且非常重要 所以这是很难戒掉的习惯

sentences.en: I know this for a fact, because a little over a year ago, I developed the habit myself.
sentences.zh: 我了解这个事实 因为一年多以前 我自己就习惯了

sentences.en: You see, my twin brother was diagnosed with stage 3 non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
sentences.zh: 你看,我的双胞胎弟弟被诊断为 第三阶段非霍奇金淋巴瘤。

sentences.en: His cancer was extremely aggressive. He had visible tumors all over his body.
sentences.zh: 他的癌症非常有攻击性 他全身都有可见的肿瘤

sentences.en: And he had to start a harsh course of chemotherapy.
sentences.zh: 他不得不开始严酷的化疗。

sentences.en: And I couldn't stop thinking about what he was going through.
sentences.zh: 我无法停止思考他正在经历的事情。

sentences.en: I couldn't stop thinking about how much he was suffering, even though he never complained, not once.
sentences.zh: 我无法停止思考他所承受的痛苦，尽管他从未抱怨过，一次也没有。

sentences.en: He had this incredibly positive attitude.
sentences.zh: 他有着令人难以置信的积极态度。

sentences.en: His psychological health was amazing. I was physically healthy, but psychologically, I was a mess.
sentences.zh: 他的心理健康状况令人惊叹。我的身体很健康，但心理上却一团糟。

sentences.en: But I knew what to do. Studies tell us that even a two-minute distraction is sufficient to break the urge to ruminate in that moment.
sentences.zh: 但我知道该怎么做。研究告诉我们，即使是两分钟的分心也足以打断那一刻沉思的冲动。

sentences.en: And so each time I had a worrying, upsetting, negative thought, I forced myself to concentrate on something else until the urge passed.
sentences.zh: 因此，每当我有令人担忧、不安、消极的想法时，我就会强迫自己专注于其他事情，直到这种冲动过去。

sentences.en: And within one week, my whole outlook changed and became more positive and more hopeful.
sentences.zh: 一周之内，我的整个看法发生了变化，变得更加积极、更加充满希望。

sentences.en: [Battle Negative Thinking] Nine weeks after he started chemotherapy, my brother had a CAT scan, and I was by his side when he got the results.
sentences.zh: [对抗消极思维] 开始化疗九周后，我哥哥做了 CAT 扫描，当他得到结果时我就在他身边。

sentences.en: All the tumors were gone. He still had three more rounds of chemotherapy to go, but we knew he would recover.
sentences.zh: 所有的肿瘤都消失了。他还需要进行三轮化疗，但我们知道他会康复。

sentences.en: This picture was taken two weeks ago. By taking action when you're lonely, by changing your responses to failure,
sentences.zh: 这张照片是两周前拍摄的。通过在孤独时采取行动，通过改变对失败的反应，

sentences.en: by protecting your self-esteem, by battling negative thinking, you won't just heal your psychological wounds, you will build emotional resilience, you will thrive.
sentences.zh: 通过保护你的自尊，通过与消极想法作斗争，你不仅会治愈你的心理创伤，你还会建立情绪恢复能力，你会茁壮成长。

sentences.en: A hundred years ago, people began practicing personal hygiene, and life expectancy rates rose by over 50 percent in just a matter of decades.
sentences.zh: 一百年前，人们开始注重个人卫生，预期寿命在短短几十年内增加了 50% 以上。

sentences.en: I believe our quality of life could rise just as dramatically if we all began practicing emotional hygiene.
sentences.zh: 我相信，如果我们都开始练习情绪卫生，我们的生活质量也会显着提高。

sentences.en: Can you imagine what the world would be like if everyone was psychologically healthier?
sentences.zh: 你能想象如果每个人的心理都更健康的话世界会是什么样子？

sentences.en: If there were less loneliness and less depression?
sentences.zh: 如果少一点孤独和抑郁呢？

sentences.en: If people knew how to overcome failure? If they felt better about themselves and more empowered?
sentences.zh: 人们是否知道如何克服失败？他们是否自我感觉更好并且更有力量？

sentences.en: If they were happier and more fulfilled?
sentences.zh: 他们是否更快乐、更满足？

sentences.en: I can, because that's the world I want to live in.
sentences.zh: 我可以，因为那是我想要生活的世界。

sentences.en: And that's the world my brother wants to live in as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我哥哥想要生活的世界。

sentences.en: And if you just become informed and change a few simple habits, well -- that's the world we can all live in.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是了解情况并改变一些简单的习惯，那么——这就是我们所有人都可以生活的世界。

sentences.en: Thank you very much. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。 （掌声）
